classification.difficultyReason: Apply the prism definition to perspective drawings, distinguishing an irregular but uniform prism from a block whose local recess changes its cross-section. This requires checking spatial structure beyond recognising familiar solids.

content.prompt: Which of the following are prisms?

spec.description: Bevelled block with matching five-sided end profiles and three hidden edges meeting at the rear lower-left vertex. Ordinary source blue and dashed red edges become black; dashed visibility is retained.
spec.mathematics: Pentagonal prism with congruent parallel end profiles.
spec.answerVisibility: Question figure only; classification is withheld.

answer.worked: The two matching pentagonal ends are parallel, and the remaining faces are parallelograms.

spec.description: Flat quadrilateral top with descending sides and rounded lower end profiles. Curved boundaries remain curved; the solid is unshaded.
spec.mathematics: The curved boundary prevents the solid being a polyhedron and hence a prism.

answer.worked: It has a curved surface, so its faces are not all polygons.

spec.description: Tall pentagonal pyramid; the two rear base vertices, rear base edges and apex connections are dashed black.
spec.mathematics: Five-sided base with triangular faces meeting at one apex.

answer.worked: Its triangular side faces meet at an apex; it does not have two congruent parallel ends.

spec.description: Oblique quadrilateral pyramid, preserving the visible diagonal between the upper-left and lower-right vertices and three dashed edges meeting at the hidden base vertex. The upper-left vertex is the pyramid apex; the uppermost vertex belongs to its base.
spec.mathematics: A quadrilateral base has four edges; four further edges join its vertices to the off-centre apex. This is not a triangular prism.

answer.worked: It is a pyramid: its triangular side faces meet at one apex rather than joining two congruent parallel ends.

spec.description: House-shaped pentagonal front end extended diagonally up and right. Rear lower and left edges are dashed; ordinary lines are black.
spec.mathematics: Congruent parallel pentagonal ends joined by parallelogram faces.

answer.worked: Its matching pentagonal ends are parallel, and its other faces are parallelograms.

spec.description: Low vertical extrusion of a stepped concave footprint. Matching top and bottom boundaries, uniform height and hidden rear lower edges are retained.
spec.mathematics: A prism may have a concave polygon as its pair of congruent parallel faces.

answer.worked: The top and bottom are congruent parallel polygons, and the connecting faces are parallelograms.

spec.description: Tall block with a local upper front-right rectangular recess. The recess has an inner vertical face and a floor, with material continuing behind it; hidden outer edges are dashed black.
spec.mathematics: The recess does not extend uniformly through the block, so the solid lacks the prism structure.

answer.worked: The local recess changes the cross-section through the block, so it does not have a uniform cross-section between matching ends.
